business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Armored Security Personnel Transport Vehicles

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Samoa – International Companies regime (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour, Companies Registry)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid – English common law foundation, local statute, and customary law (Fa'asamoa)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Pacific Agreement on Closer Economic Relations (PACER Plus, 2017, in force)
WTO General Agreement on Trade in Services (GATS)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 (as amended) and Money Laundering Prevention Regulations; International Companies Act 1987 (No. 4 of 1987, as amended); Financial Intelligence Unit powers; AML/CFT obligations of licensed registered agents under APG mutual evaluation requirements
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access – beneficial ownership records are held by the licensed registered agent, are not publicly searchable, and are accessible by the Registrar of Companies, the Financial Intelligence Unit, and Samoa Police upon lawful request; nominee arrangements are permissible only when the true UBO is disclosed to the registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference and source-of-funds letter for each ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution in the account-holder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized banker's attestation with Hague Apostille (or consular legalization)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police clearance certificate or PEP declaration for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or designated government authority of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary or governing body of the shareholder entity

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, UBOs, and counterparties against the OFAC SDN List, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UK HMT sanctions list, and Samoa domestic designations under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; PEPs require enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, senior-management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring; defense-sector counterparties are additionally screened for arms embargoes and end-use risk.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) – Companies Registry, International Companies Unit; applications filed through MCIL-licensed registered agents using the official company registration portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory registered name must be in Roman alphabetic characters and end with 'Limited' or 'Ltd' (or approved abbreviation). A Chinese-language trading name may be adopted internally in the constitutional documents only where a certified pinyin/English transliteration is lodged with the Registrar; the official registered name remains the Roman-script name. The name must not be identical or deceptively similar to an existing Samoa company, IC, or reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: A reservation may be renewed once for an additional 30 days by written application through the registered agent before expiry. Upon rejection, a written appeal with legal grounds must be filed with the Registrar of Companies within 14 days of the refusal notice; if the appeal is dismissed, a fresh name application with a distinct proposed name may be submitted. Sensitive tokens in the permitted list require prior written approval of the responsible Minister or regulator before filing.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A Samoa International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa, which may be the office of the licensed registered agent; a virtual office satisfies only the legal-address requirement. The IC is prohibited under the International Companies Act 1987 from carrying on a domestic trading or manufacturing business in Samoa, and the ISIC 3040 armored-vehicle manufacturing operation must therefore have its physical production, inventory, and personnel substance in the host jurisdiction. A purely paper Samoan address would create a deficient commercial-substance profile for a high-risk defense entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% per annum) for the Samoa registered office, which is subject to Registrar compliance checks upon complaint, adverse information, or regulatory request; the offshore manufacturing site carries a markedly higher unannounced-inspection risk due to the defense-licensing regime and is governed by host-state authorities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; ss.5–15 (incorporation and certificate of incorporation), s.19 (registered office), s.27 (first directors); International Companies (Fees) Regulations 1998
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International and Foreign Companies, International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Certificate of Incorporation issued upon filing of the Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1) together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for a Samoa International Company; authorized capital is stated in the Articles of Association (commonly US$1,000 divided into ordinary shares). No escrow account or up-front capital deposit is required at incorporation; shares may be issued fully or partly paid, with consideration determined by the first directors.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION of [Company Name] Limited. RESOLVED that the initial subscription of 1,000 ordinary shares at US$1.00 each by the founding subscriber be accepted, allotted, and credited as fully paid in the register of members. RESOLVED that the registered office at [Registered Agent Address], Apia, Samoa, is adopted as the statutory registered office, and the licensed registered agent is authorized to accept service of process. RESOLVED that [Director A], [Director B], and [Director C] are appointed first Directors, and [Secretary] is appointed Secretary, under the Articles. RESOLVED that the Directors may open bank accounts and secure all licenses required for the Company's defense manufacturing operations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed international company service provider, submit a name-reservation application to the Registrar via the approved electronic portal or the Registry counter, specify the proposed corporate name, and reserve the name for 30 days while the application dossier is prepared.
required_dossiers: Copy of the founding subscriber's passport
Proof of engagement of the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused for conflict or objectionable character, file an administrative request for review under the International Companies Act 1987 and submit two alternative names for accelerated re-screening.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed International Company Services Provider / Registered Agent, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) standards
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, incorporating a special objects clause covering the manufacture of armored security personnel transport vehicles and all lawful ancillary defense-tactical hardware activities; the founding subscriber executes the document before a notary public, with signature pages attested and the registered agent executing consent.
required_dossiers: Memorandum and Articles of Association (signed and notarized)
Certificate of non-conflict for the corporate name
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If notarization or attestation is defective, the subscriber re-executes corrected signature pages without regeneration of the full document; any objectional articles are amended before filing at no additional statutory fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Application for Incorporation (Form IC-1)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-1 Application for Incorporation at the International Companies Registry, either by physical counter submission at Apia or via the registered agent's authenticated electronic channel, attaching the executed Memorandum and Articles, a declaration of compliance, and the registered agent consent; all documents must be in English with certified copies where applicable.
required_dossiers: Declaration of compliance signed by the founding subscriber
Certified passport copies of directors and subscribers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry issues a defect notice or query, cure by filing supplementary information or corrected forms within 14 days; if the query challenges the defense-objects clause, provide written explanation of the regulatory licensing plan and amend the articles if formally required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Finance Section, Apia, Samoa
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Effect payment of the US$150 official state filing fee by bank telegraphic transfer to the designated MCIL government revenue account or by cashier's cheque at the Registry cashier, quoting the application reference number; retain the official receipt for attachment to the application file.
required_dossiers: Bank telegraphic transfer receipt or cashier's cheque
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If payment is misallocated or rejected, request a reconciliation memorandum from the MCIL Finance Section, obtain a credit note, and re-remit with a corrected payment reference; no re-filing of the substantive application is required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Filing Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, International Companies Registry, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon satisfactory examination of the application and confirmation of fee payment, the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation and an extract of registered particulars; the company is incorporated as of the certificate date; thereafter establish the statutory registers of members, directors, and charges at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Certificate of Incorporation contains minor clerical errors, apply to the Registrar for rectification under the International Companies Act 1987; if issuance is delayed beyond SLA, escalate to the Registrar and request expedition upon payment of the standard priority fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Governance and Commencement of Ancillary Licensing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Directors and Licensed Registered Agent; Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) for follow-on registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass a written resolution adopting the First Board Resolution, confirm initial share allotment and officer appointments, approve the authorized signatories for bank and government filings, and instruct counsel to commence applications for the manufacturing business licence, factory registration, and any defense-tactical import or production permits required by the Samoa Police Service.
required_dossiers: Consent to act forms of directors and secretary
Draft business licence and factory registration applications
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank applies enhanced AML/KYC review because of the defense-tactical scope, supplement the file with ultimate beneficial ownership declarations, economic substance statements, and the approved licensing roadmap; if the business licence is queried, coordinate with MCIL and the Samoa Police Service to narrow the licensed scope pending full environmental and civil defense clearances.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) — Business Licences Division and Labour/Occupational Safety Division; with statutory coordination of the Samoa Police Service (Commissioner of Police) for defense-tactical hardware production permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Business Licence (Manufacturing of Armored Security Personnel Transport Vehicles) under the Business Licences Act 2016, together with Factory Registration Certificate under the Factories and Industrial Safety Act 1972

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) — Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Full EIA Report (Category C) — mandatory for industrial manufacturing and metal fabrication facilities under the Planning and Urban Management Act 2004
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must comply with Samoa/WHO ambient standards (BOD5 ≤ 50 mg/L, TSS ≤ 50 mg/L, pH 6.5–8.5); VOC emissions from painting and coating lines must use low-VOC materials and controlled ventilation with solvent recovery; all hazardous waste, including spent solvents, paint sludge, and used batteries, must be manifested and transported by a licensed waste carrier under the Waste Management Act 2005.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (FESA) covering building fire suppression and evacuation systems; structural clearance by the MCIL Building Inspectorate under the Samoa National Building Code; factory and workplace clearance by the Labour Division (MCIL) under the Factories and Industrial Safety Act 1972; additional police security clearance and high-risk trade authorization from the Commissioner of Police for production and custody of tactical-grade vehicle components.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa (MfR), 'Lapau' Internal Revenue Division, Apia – official portal: https://www.mfr.gov.ws; offshore International Companies are additionally registered and regulated by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia – https://www.sifa.gov.ws.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: A licensed SIFA-registered agent files the proposed company name and constitutional documents with the Registrar of International Companies. Step 2: Upon incorporation, SIFA issues the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the International Company register number and authorized capital details; this certificate serves as the statutory tax identification instrument for the offshore regime. Step 3: If the IC engages in any taxable domestic supply or imports goods into Samoa, the IC must separately apply to the Ministry for Revenue for a VAGST registration number (TN) and an income tax number (TIN) on Form MFR-VAGST-REG and MFR-TIN-APP, providing the certificate, local registered office, and agent details. Step 4: For the zero-rated defense export channel, the IC files a customs client registration through ASYCUDA World at the Ministry for Revenue and Customs. Step 5: The IC must appoint a local registered agent and maintain a registered office in Samoa throughout its existence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Tax_Exempt_Zone – Samoa International Companies are statutory non-resident offshore entities. They are exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty, and all other Samoan taxes on offshore/international business income, including income from the manufacture and export of military tactical vehicles to non-resident defense buyers. The IC is not taxed on world income derived outside Samoa, and no withholding tax applies on distributions to non-resident shareholders. Local-source business in Samoa is prohibited and would forfeit the exemption.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box regime exists in Samoa. Elections available: (1) An IC may elect in its constitution to be a 'company limited by guarantee' or 'company limited by shares' and may alter its authorized capital, with corresponding changes to the annual SIFA fee; (2) An IC may elect to convert into an ordinary company under the Companies Act 2001 or into a foreign company, thereby waiving the offshore tax exemption and becoming taxable under the Income Tax Act 2012; (3) An IC may elect to issue shares in any currency and maintain accounts in a foreign currency, which reinforces its non-resident, tax-exempt character; (4) No hybrid mismatch election is available under Samoan law; Samoa has adopted only limited BEPS-aligned rules that do not presently override the IC exemption.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax) – a GST-style consumption tax imposed under the Value Added Goods and Services Tax Act 1992, administered by the Ministry for Revenue, and applied at importation and on domestic supplies of goods and services.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 – compulsory VAGST registration is triggered when taxable supplies in Samoa exceed WST 100,000 in any 12-month period. International Companies that only make offshore supplies remain outside the VAGST net; registration is voluntary for annual taxable turnover below WST 100,000 but is required to claim input credits on local procurement.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa has no mandatory real-time electronic invoicing, fiscal clearance, API filing, or digital stamping regime. Registered persons must issue a standard tax invoice under VAGST Act 1992 section 32 containing the supplier name and address, VAGST registration number, invoice number, date of supply, description, quantity, price, and VAGST amount. Defense export invoices are contractual documents supporting customs clearance via ASYCUDA World; no digital stamp is affixed by the tax authority.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of tangible movable goods, including all-terrain armored military tactical vehicles classified under ISIC 3040, are zero-rated under VAGST Act 1992 section 14 when the goods are exported by the supplier or for the supplier's account within 28 days of supply and are not subsequently re-imported. Zero-rating also extends to freight, insurance, and handling services directly related to the exported vehicles, as well as services physically performed on movable goods for export (e.g., military fit-out and armor installation) when performed for a non-resident recipient. Defense end-use requires an export authorization under Samoa's Exchange Control Act 1975 and applicable arms export permits; failure to produce the end-user certificate and destination certificate invalidates the zero-rated claim.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EDN) filed via ASYCUDA World by the IC or its licensed customs broker
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill evidencing physical export of the vehicles to the foreign defense buyer
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or SWIFT MT103 issued by an authorized dealer confirming receipt of foreign currency proceeds
Tax invoice meeting VAGST Act 1992 section 32 requirements with an explicit zero-rated supply notation
End-User Certificate and export permit for military tactical hardware issued by the relevant Samoan authority
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue and the Central Bank of Samoa may retrospectively audit export zero-rating claims where the goods are not exported within 28 days, the proceeds are not received within 180 days, or documentation is deficient or fraudulent. Clawback is measured at the standard 15% VAGST rate on the full supply value, plus interest. Penalties under the VAGST Act 1992 and the Tax Administration Act 2012 include shortfall penalties up to 150% of the tax evaded for deliberate concealment, civil penalties for each false statement, and criminal fines and imprisonment for officers in the case of fraudulent zero-rating schemes. The Customs Service may also suspend the IC's export license and require security or guarantees for future shipments. For International Companies, abuse of the offshore exemption through fictitious export transactions additionally triggers revocation of the IC status by SIFA, rendering the entity taxable on all income from inception.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), operating under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984 and the Exchange Control Act 1973; delegated authority for exchange control administration and enforcement.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is not freely convertible offshore. Current account payments are generally permitted through authorized dealers, but capital account transactions require CBS prior approval. Profit remittance from a non-resident International Company (IC) is unrestricted if funded by offshore foreign currency source and not involving resident counterparties; however, any conversion to WST for local settlement triggers CBS documentation requirements. ICs operating purely in foreign currency with no local revenue face low remittance friction.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Resident exporters must surrender foreign exchange export proceeds to an authorized dealer within six months from shipment and convert to WST unless an exemption is granted by CBS. Non-resident International Companies are automatically exempt from surrender and conversion obligations when export receivables are denominated in foreign currency and are not derived from resident business or local currency resources. The IC should maintain a CBS approval letter or SIFA-issued exemption certificate to evidence compliance.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Rating: Low. Samoa does not operate a digital EMI (Electronic Money Institution) licensing regime. Offshore fintech firms providing cross-border payment services are not authorized to clear through Samoa’s real-time gross settlement or local interbank rails. Such EMIs may be used incidentally for ancillary payments via overseas correspondent banks, but cannot serve as a primary liquidity or clearing conduit for the IC.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote account opening is generally permissible for a Samoa International Company with non-resident directors, provided certified true copies of constitutional documents, notarized board resolutions, and valid passport copies are submitted. However, for a high-risk defense-sector entity, CBS-compliant banks may enforce a discretionary requirement for at least one director or a senior officer to attend an in-person interview at the bank’s Apia head office before activating a capital escrow account. There is no statutory mandate, but practical onboarding for this sector almost always requires physical attendance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry-sector red flag (ISIC 3040 – military vehicle manufacturing) triggering enhanced due diligence, sanctions and proliferation financing screening.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: A complete dossier including: (i) government-issued end-user certificates; (ii) verified Ministry of Defense or diplomatic purchase order contracts; (iii) Samoa Export License or SIFA approval for defense-tactical goods; (iv) company AML/CTF policy aligned with FATF Recommendations; (v) a transaction flow diagram for all proposed counterparties.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial ownership (UBO) and sanctions screening flags arising from an offshore family trust or nominee structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed UBO declarations with source-of-wealth evidence; an organizational ownership chart; World-Check or Dow Jones screening results for each director and owner; certified passports of trustees and beneficiaries; and an independent legal opinion confirming no OFAC/EU/Samoa sanctions nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds ambiguity for large inbound capital injections from a military-industrial trust or overseas parent.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited financial statements of the parent or trust for the preceding two years; bank reference letters from the originating bank; notarized trust deed and trustee acceptance; evidence of lawful origin such as licensed arms manufacturing contracts; a formal source-of-funds attestation by the IC’s registered agent.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Residency and tax status inconsistency of a Samoa International Company that claims tax-exempt status while maintaining significant economic activity.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation, Certificate of Good Standing, and current tax exemption certificate issued by the Samoa Ministry of Revenue; SIFA license or registration confirmation; a legal opinion confirming that the IC is non-resident under Samoa’s Exchange Control Act; and a detailed indication of the offshore bookkeeping and management location.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant routing for inbound capital injections: a SWIFT MT103 from the overseas parent or trust to the IC’s foreign currency operational account at a licensed Samoa bank, referencing Exchange Control Form R-1 or a CBS inward remittance approval number. The purpose code must align with an appropriate OECD BOP code, e.g., 682 (direct investment in equity capital) or 911 (proceeds from disposal of fixed assets) for trust distributions. For capital injections exceeding WST 1,000,000 equivalent, a prior CBS capital account approval is mandatory. Verification package includes the board resolution approving the injection, source-of-funds evidence, and SIFA endorsement confirming the IC’s offshore status.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary clearing rails for trade settlements: (i) SWIFT MT103/MT202 COV for direct supplier payments under open-account terms, especially to approved defense-component suppliers; (ii) Commercial Letters of Credit (usance or sight) issued via SWIFT MT700/MT720, with the Samoa bank acting solely as advising/confirming bank if the IC is the beneficiary; (iii) for government and diplomatic purchasers, irrevocable diplomatic LC advised through a top-tier international bank with MT103 settlement after presentation of delivery certificates and E.U.C. For all outbound disbursements, the IC must retain approved end-user certificates, customs manifest, and proof of licensed export to satisfy CBS reporting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable forwards against WST (maximum tenor 12 months) through a CBS-authorized dealer
Offshore non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) in USD/WST for non-resident ICs, settled in USD
Cross-currency swaps (USD/WST) for capital transactions, subject to CBS prior approval
Interest rate swaps on trade-related borrowings, provided the underlying exposure is a qualifying defense export receivable

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Government Fee (International Company Annual Fee)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before each anniversary of incorporation; payable annually from the date of registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-payment surcharge on overdue fee; if unpaid for 3 months after the due date, the Registrar may strike the company off the register; restoration only by court order with reinstatement fees

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return (Confirmation Statement) of Members, Directors, Registered Office and Registered Agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies, MCIL, Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days after each anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Daily/monthly late filing penalties imposed on the company and registered agent for default; persistent non-filing constitutes grounds for administrative strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Confirmation Filed with Annual Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registrar of International Companies / Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU), Samoa
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Simultaneously with the annual return within 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Corporate fines up to WST 100,000 under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter Financing of Terrorism Act 2018; personal liability on directors and the registered agent for false or omitted UBO declarations

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Renewal of Special Statutory License (Defense / Tactical Hardware Sector Endorsement)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Sector Licensing Authority, MCIL, Samoa (in coordination with Customs and Trade Control)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of license issuance; must be renewed before 31 December of each calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Automatic suspension of the license; prohibition on production, export, and import of all-terrain military tactical vehicles; possible revocation of export permits and forfeiture of bonded inventory

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No mandatory statutory audit for a standard Samoa International Company; audit is compulsory only if the company holds a banking, insurance, or trust license, or if shareholders representing at least 10% of the issued shares demand an audit; defense-sector government contract terms may independently require an agreed-upon procedures or compliance audit
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as routinely adopted; no filing of financial statements with the Registrar is required for tax-exempt International Companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Register of Beneficial Owners must be kept at the registered office; any share transfer, allotment, or change in ultimate beneficial ownership during the year must be recorded and confirmed in the annual UBO declaration; changes to UBOs must be updated in the register within 14 days of the transaction
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Minute Book (General Meetings and Director Resolutions)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 4,000 - 10,000 per annum if triggered (not mandatory for exempt International Companies)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for ordinary resident companies (Income Tax Act 2015); 0% for International Companies (ICs) registered under the International Companies Act 1987 (ICA 1987), which are tax-exempt on all qualifying offshore income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full income tax exemption under ICA 1987 s.159: no corporate income tax, no capital gains tax, no dividend withholding tax, no stamp duty on share transfers, and no annual income-based taxation. An IC may obtain a Tax Exemption Certificate from the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), producing a 0% effective rate on the restricted offshore business scope of the IC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return — Form prescribed under Part X of the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended); filed electronically through the SIFA eRegistry by the licensed Samoa registered agent.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 30 days after each anniversary of the date of incorporation; the annual license fee (based on authorized capital) is payable simultaneously. No extension is ordinarily granted; a 14-day grace period applies before late penalties accrue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered company name and registration number as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors must verify the exact registered name; the Samoa registered agent signs and lodges the return; electronic submission suffices and no notarization is required.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registered office address and registered agent details in Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be maintained by a SIFA-licensed registered agent; non-resident beneficial owners cannot act as registered agent or registered office provider.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Current register of directors and shareholders, including passport copies and ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) declaration.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents provide scanned passports and proof of address; the UBO declaration is held confidentially by the registered agent and is not publicly filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Compliance declaration confirming the IC has not carried on business in Samoa, held Samoan real property, or conducted banking or insurance with Samoan residents.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Declared by a director under penalty of perjury. For an ISIC 3040 offshore manufacturer, the declaration confirms all production, procurement, and sales contracts are concluded and executed outside Samoa.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prescribed annual fee calculation and Tax Exemption Certificate reference number.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The annual fee is remitted by the registered agent from client funds; the certificate under ICA 1987 s.159 confirms 0% corporate income tax, 0% withholding tax, and 0% stamp duty.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an initial administrative penalty (approximately SAT 250) plus a daily default surcharge (approximately SAT 20 per day); a further late-fee surcharge of up to 10% of the annual fee applies after 60 days; prolonged default leads to strike-off and dissolution, a restoration fee of up to SAT 5,000, and referral of director information to Samoa's Ministry of Revenue for international information exchange.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Tax Exemption Certificate Application under s.159, International Companies Act 1987 — submitted to the Registrar of International Companies through SIFA (paper or eRegistry).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Once at incorporation; renewed when the exemption period lapses or when the IC's business scope changes in a manner affecting the exemption.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No fixed statutory filing deadline; best practice requires the certificate to be obtained before the first income is received and renewed within 6 months of any material change in business scope.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Company name, registration number, and date of incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Entry must exactly match the SIFA registry data; the registered agent prepares the form based on incorporation documents.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Intended business activities — manufacture of armored security personnel transport vehicles (ISIC 3040).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Describe the offshore manufacturing, export sales to governments, and diplomatic procurement channels; confirm that no income is derived from Samoa sources.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement that management and control are exercised outside Samoa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Board resolutions and shareholder decisions should be executed outside Samoa; signed minutes must be forwarded to the Samoa registered agent for retention.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Undertaking to file the annual return and pay the annual fee.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The registered agent gives this undertaking on behalf of non-resident directors, together with the continuous power of attorney from the IC.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Carrying on business without a valid Tax Exemption Certificate after a material change invites revocation of the exemption; benefits are clawed back by assessment at 25% on Samoan-source receipts plus penalties up to 100% of the tax avoided.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Samoa's statutory dividend withholding tax is 20% for dividends paid by ordinary resident companies to non-residents (Income Tax Act 2015). An International Company is fully exempt from this tax: distributions by the IC to its non-resident shareholders carry 0% Samoa dividend withholding tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Where a non-IC payer is involved, treaty relief requires: (1) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the Samoan Ministry of Revenue or the foreign treaty partner; (2) lodge Samoa's withholding tax treaty-relief application with the Commissioner, attaching the TRC and a beneficial-ownership declaration; (3) await the Commissioner's reduced-rate certificate before payment is made to the foreign payee; and (4) file the certificate with the resident payer. Samoa's DTA network is narrow, the principal full treaties being with Australia and New Zealand, which can reduce dividend rates to 15% or lower, interest to 10%, and royalties to 15%. For a tax-exempt IC repatriating dividends, no DTA filing is required because the IC is already at 0% Samoa tax.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: For ordinary resident payers, statutory withholding rates are 15% on interest and 15% on royalties (Income Tax Act 2015); technical and management fees may be subject to a separate 10% non-resident contractor withholding. Treaty rates may apply (e.g., Australia-Samoa DTA: interest 10%, royalties 15%). For an International Company paying royalties or interest to non-residents, the Samoa rate is 0% because the IC's payment flows are outside the Samoa income tax and withholding tax statutory net.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No explicit WST monetary threshold is gazetted in Samoa's Income Tax Act 2015. In administrative practice, the Ministry of Revenue expects contemporaneous Master File and Local File documentation where cross-border related-party turnover exceeds approximately WST 1,000,000 per annum. A tax-exempt International Company is excluded from the Samoan corporate income tax net and therefore owes no Samoan TP documentation; if the IC's exemption is revoked, TP documentation becomes mandatory from the first year of taxable status.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Samoa applies economic substance rules under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Act 2020, enacted following Samoa's EU listing review. An IC carrying on a 'relevant activity' — banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, distribution and service centers, holding-company functions, or intellectual-property holding/development — must meet Samoa substance tests, including physical presence, locally based decision-making, and adequate employees and expenditure. Manufacture of armored security personnel transport vehicles (ISIC 3040) is not a listed relevant activity; the IC is therefore outside the enhanced substance regime as long as it confines itself to offshore manufacturing, export logistics, and government/diplomatic procurement. The IC must still keep board minutes, registries, and records at the Samoa registered office and must respond to the annual economic substance notification where directed by SIFA. If the IC owns product-related IP and derives royalty income from that IP within an intra-group arrangement, the high-value IP core-income tests can apply and would require demonstrable strategic functions, personnel, and decision-making in Samoa.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion and Abusive Use of the International Company Exemption
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Conducting actual trading activities with Samoan residents, deriving income sourced in Samoa, or using the IC as a mere shell with fictitious board minutes and artificial offshore management records to claim the 0% IC rate.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Revocation of the Tax Exemption Certificate; back-assessment at 25% corporate income tax on undeclared Samoan-source income for up to 8 years; late payment penalties and daily surcharges; strike-off and cancellation of IC registration; denial of treaty benefits and mandatory exchange of information with foreign tax authorities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may face personal liability for unpaid tax where the corporate veil is pierced; fines up to SAT 100,000; imprisonment up to 5 years for false statutory declarations; travel/exit restriction orders may be issued while tax liabilities remain outstanding; disqualification from acting as a director of any Samoa company.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT Violations on Defense-Tactical Hardware Flows
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to conduct customer/supplier due diligence, dealing with sanctioned states or designated persons, accepting undisclosed third-party funds, or omitting the UBO declaration while receiving government wire payments and diplomatic letters of credit for armored vehicle sales.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Samoa's AML/CFT regime, corporate fines up to SAT 500,000 and employee fines up to SAT 200,000 per violation; freezing and forfeiture of assets; cancellation of the special defense-hardware license; referral to the Financial Intelligence Unit and foreign enforcement counterparts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors knowingly involved face imprisonment up to 14 years, personal financial penalties, travel bans to prevent flight, and confiscation orders over personal assets; professional debarment of the registered agent may follow a breach of reporting obligations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Unlicensed Defense Manufacturing and Export Control Breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Exporting or procuring all-terrain military tactical vehicles without the required statutory license and strategic-goods permit, falsifying end-user certificates, or routing controlled equipment through a third-country intermediary without authorization.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Confiscation and forfeiture of the goods; fines up to SAT 1,000,000; suspension and permanent blacklisting of the IC from Samoan registry benefits; cancellation of the special license; possible referral for criminal prosecution under trade-control legislation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors face criminal conviction and imprisonment for unlawful export of defense hardware; civil restitution to affected parties; personal disqualification orders; departure prohibition and asset seizure to enforce judgments.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Regulatory Default: Non-Filing and False Substance Representation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the International Company Annual Return, non-payment of SIFA annual fees, non-lodgment of the economic substance notification where applicable, and absence of records at the Samoa registered office.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Registrar may strike off and dissolve the IC; late penalty fees accrue daily; the IC loses the protection of limited liability for obligations incurred after dissolution; restoration requires payment of arrears, penalties, and a restoration fee of up to SAT 5,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who consented to trading while the company is dissolved may be held personally liable for company debts; sanctions include director disqualification, fines for continued non-compliance, and potential criminal liability for knowingly making false compliance declarations.
